items.title: Workers who lose their jobs to AI say they're also addicted to using it
paras: Oksana is a micro drama actor who has lost work to AI-generated shows. ( ABC News: Allyson Horn )
The 26-year-old was booked back-to-back to work on short-drama projects, usually bite-sized serialised videos made specifically for mobile viewing.
But this year, that work has all but disappeared because of the rise of videos produced with artificial intelligence (AI).
"Many of the companies I used to know and work with have switched to AI and no longer shoot live-action dramas," she said.
"If I wanted to, I previously could have kept shooting until I dropped dead.
In 2026, more than 90 per cent of China's new micro dramas were generated by AI, including the actors, voices and scenes.
Rather than a whole crew and set, micro dramas can be made by very small teams on computers in a studio. ( ABC )
Government figures show about 1,600 new AI micro dramas launched every day for the first half of 2026.
The AI videos have become so popular that even someone like Oksana, who has lost her job to the technology, is "obsessed" with them.
"With those two or 300-episode short dramas, once I click in, I forget about getting out.
"Even when I go to sleep each night, I leave the sound on and fall asleep listening.
"My head is a bit of a mess every day now, and I can't focus on anything else."
The micro drama episodes often focus on fantasy, underdog-style or romantic storylines alongside time-travelling and urban dramas.
The episodes are usually free and end on cliffhangers designed to keep people watching, with viewers having to pay to see the rest of the series.
One of China's biggest hits of 2026, drawing 6.08 billion views, is a series where a woman wakes up in the Tang dynasty and gains power by slaying demons that roam the city.
AI-generated videos of pets and anthropomorphic fruit are also finding large audiences.
AI micro drama developer Zhu Zhili said the technology allowed companies to produce entertainment content quicker, cheaper and with more advanced storylines.
"Before, we needed to hire real actors, build sets, go into studios, and so on," he said.
Zhu Zhili says AI makes production much more efficient. ( ABC News: Allyson Horn )
"Now, with AI, we only need a very small team working together on computers in a company or studio to produce a short drama that previously would have taken enormous manpower and resources to shoot.
"We can just use AI to do the pictures, storyboard generation, generative audio, generative music, and generative voiceover.
AI creators have reported dramas may cost about one-tenth of traditional live-action shoots.
But Mr Zhu said despite the large volume of new dramas being made, turning a profit could still be difficult.
"In the first half of this year, China produced a total of 220,000 AI short dramas, which is an enormous number," he said.
"But on the other hand, only about 1,000 of them truly broke out, meaning they succeeded, passed 100 million views, or made money, a share of less than 0.4 per cent."
Zhu Zhili uses AI for pictures, storyboarding and generative audio, music and voiceover. ( ABC News: Allyson Horn )
China has ambitious goals to have AI agents, devices and applications reach 90 per cent penetration in key sectors by 2030.
The government's current five-year plan also lists micro dramas as an emerging form of "cultural business" to be actively developed.
The AI entertainment industry's development has moved at breakneck speed since the release of powerful new AI video software, like tech group ByteDance's Seedance 2.0 model.
But Chinese social media is full of stories and complaints by former actors who are now out of work.

"Then this year, after AI became widespread, nearly all my peers stopped getting call sheets. I've been at home without work for several months too," said user Liu Yuzhan, who now works as a delivery driver.
Oksana says it's a similar story among her industry friends, but she believes there will always be an appetite for real human acting in longer-form content.
"Many of my peers have switched to livestreaming because of the current environment and can no longer work as professional actors," she said.
"It can never replace live actors, or the imperfections in their acting and their subtle emotions.

items.title: Baby bill shock: Data matching whacks tens of thousands of taxpayers
paras: Advertisement Business Consumer affairs Health insurance Baby bill shock: Data matching whacks tens of thousands of taxpayers Madeleine Heffernan November 28, 2026 — 11:55am
You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month.

Share A A A Tens of thousands of Australians are being snared in a Tax Office push on private health insurance, and are forced to pay thousands in Medicare levy surcharge despite having private cover.
The Australian Taxation Office is using data matching technology to enforce a poorly understood law on families’ private health insurance.

Now, about 50,000 people are staring down hefty tax debts for not taking out private hospital cover for all family members, including dependent children and spouses, or buying the wrong kind of insurance.

Forget to get private health insurance for your baby and you’ll have to pay a surcharge. Getty Lisa Greig, a tax lecturer at the University of Melbourne, said the number of affected taxpayers was surprisingly large, and probably caused by a misunderstanding of how the laws apply or a lack of attention to detail in tax return disclosures, rather than tax avoidance.

Some parents agree and have complained they were not informed – by their tax agent, insurer or the hospital where they gave birth – that they needed to add their child to their insurance to avoid a pricey surcharge.

The ATO has not yet determined the total amount owed. It is also unclear what the average debt is, although people are reporting receiving bills in the thousands. In the 2024 financial year, 885,087 people paid the Medicare levy surcharge, at an average $1284 per person.

The Australian Taxation Office is using data matching technology to enforce a poorly understood law on private health insurance. Louie Douvis In July, the Tax Office flagged it would send “data matching letters” to well-paid people or families who did not have the required “appropriate level of private patient hospital insurance” to avoid the Medicare levy surcharge. “Appropriate” cover must have an excess of $750 or less for singles, while couples or families must have an excess of $1500 or less. General cover, known as extras, does not qualify.

The surcharge is designed to encourage people on high incomes to take out private hospital cover and applies to singles earning at least $105,000, and couples and families earning at least $210,000 combined. It’s levied at between 1 per cent and 1.5 per cent of income, and kicks in if any family member – even dependent children, such as newborns – does not have “an appropriate level of private patient hospital cover”. (The surcharge is in addition to the 2 per cent Medicare levy most taxpayers already pay.)

This week, the ATO said it “expect[ed] to issue letters to approximately 50,000 taxpayers based on data related to the 2025-income year, following comparisons between information reported in taxpayers’ tax returns, private health insurance records and spouse tax return information”.

“This population includes taxpayers not holding an appropriate level of cover for themselves and/or their family, [and] instances where information reported by private health insurers does not match information reported by the taxpayer,” it said.

The ATO is asking parents whether their children have hospital insurance. Dom Lorrimer The ATO reminded taxpayers they were “responsible for ensuring the information reported in their tax return is accurate and reflects their personal and family circumstances”.

Greig said: “Many people assume that holding their own hospital cover means they’re saved from the Medicare levy surcharge. But if you have a spouse or a dependent child, the test is whether everyone in the family is covered. Unfortunately, both spouses can get caught with paying, even the taxpayer with the cover.”

Mark Chapman of H&R Block says health insurers can help prevent bill shock. An ATO spokesperson said taxpayers could avoid unexpected Medicare levy surcharge liabilities by reviewing their insurance statements, checking their cover includes all dependents and speaking to their tax agent. Insurance experts say the levy is more expensive than the hospital cover.

The surcharge is not new, but its underpayment has become more apparent under data matching. “With the ATO matching insurer data against tax returns, mistakes are being picked up,” said Jenny Wong, the tax lead at accounting organisation CPA Australia.
Wong advised people who have been contacted by the ATO to “check the schedule carefully against their own records, talk to their tax agent and respond before the due date if they disagree”.

Mark Chapman, the director of tax communications at accounting firm H&R Block Australia, said the Medicare levy surcharge was not well-known, and it was unreasonable for the ATO to expect people to understand tax law without outside help.
“There has to be an obligation on particularly the insurance companies to advise them of their obligations to make sure that everybody is actually covered under the policy,” Chapman said.
“There’s a real weakness there in terms of the burden basically falling entirely on taxpayers to disclose this information.”

But the Australian Health Funds Council, which represents private health insurance funds, said health funds “were very clear on the requirement”, and acknowledged people would seek advice about health insurance and the Medicare Levy surcharges. “We would hope and expect that brokers, financial advisers and others are giving accurate advice to customers,” a spokesperson for the council said.

They said that if people used their health insurance when starting or expanding a family, their fund “may invite” them to add their baby to the policy. But under Australian taxation law, they said, “the onus is on the individual to know about the Medicare levy surcharge and dependents”.

The letters highlight an increasing reliance by the ATO on data provided by third parties, such as health insurers, banks, land agencies, crypto platforms, temporary accommodation providers and government departments, to ensure people are paying the right amount of tax.

“The data’s just so rich now, so their data matching is getting better and better,” said Greig, who predicts more people will get ATO letters to review and amend their tax returns – for various reasons beyond health insurance – based on discrepancies found through data matching.

items.title: What to expect with Victoria's election count tonight
paras: The key question is whether the Coalition can win majority government in Victoria. ( ABC News: Cordelia Brown )
Barring an unprecedented polling miss, Victorian Labor is set to be defeated after 12 years in government.
The Coalition is likely to form majority government, in an election that could deliver one of the most complex results in Australian political history.
The final makeup of parliament remains anyone's guess, including the number of One Nation MPs — and how influential they'll be in the next parliament.
You can follow the results using the live results service on the ABC's website .
We will be bringing you the latest figures and helping you make sense of the numbers from the ABC Election Centre in Melbourne.
The state election results will be complicated by One Nation's rise and record-low polling for Labor. ( ABC News: Danielle Bonica )
More than 1,700 polling centres across Victoria will close at 6pm AEDT.
The first figures are expected to come in within an hour of polls closing.
If the polls are correct, we may be able to project which party will have the best chance of forming government early in the night.
But the results in each one of the 88 Legislative Assembly districts may not be known until the full distribution of preferences are completed in the second week of December.
To give us an indication of the result before that process is completed, electoral commissions do two-candidate preferred counts.
This means the Victorian Electoral Commission (VEC) must pick the two candidates they believe will come first and second.
More than 1,700 polling centres across Victoria will close at 6pm before counting begins. ( ABC News: Patrick Stone )
One Nation's rise and record-low polling for Labor make it much harder to make those decisions.
If it looks like the VEC's prediction is not correct, the ABC will estimate preference flows to project the two-candidate preferred figure.
Those estimates are based on our analysis of historical voting patterns.
To win majority government, the Coalition will need to win 16 additional seats and not lose any of the ones it holds.
Liberal leader Jess Wilson, who holds the seat of Kew, hopes to be Victoria's next premier. ( AAP: Con Chronis )
Despite the Coalition's improvement in the polls through the campaign, One Nation is still in contention to win Coalition seats and snatch gains in marginal Labor seats.

The Nationals-held seat of Morwell is considered among One Nation's best hopes of winning any seat in Victoria and the seats of Hastings and Bass on Western Port Bay, narrowly held by Labor, are not far behind.
The same is true of Pakenham in Melbourne's outer east, where state leader Warren Pickering is running.
One Nation's leader in Victoria, Warren Pickering, is running to win the seat of Pakenham. ( AAP: Joel Carrett )
If One Nation is doing well, the Coalition's other path to majority government runs through Melbourne's north and west.
The Coalition hasn't won a seat north or west of the Yarra since 1996 so if it is leading in safe Labor seats like Greenvale , Tarneit or Eltham then it is probably on track for a very good night.
Premier Ben Carroll appears highly vulnerable in his seat of Niddrie in Melbourne's north-west, so many within Labor will be keeping an eye on which leadership contenders hold on.
Deputy Premier Gabrielle Williams holds the safe Labor seat of Dandenong and her opponent for the deputy leadership position in July, Steve Dimopoulos, holds Oakleigh .
Labor losing either of those seats would represent an utter electoral disaster.
Labor's deputy leader Gabrielle Williams and leader Ben Carroll hold the seats of Dandenong and Niddrie. ( ABC News: Danielle Bonica )
Voters in Victoria are also casting their vote for the Legislative Council, the state's upper house.

While the final composition of the upper house is going to be hard to determine on the night, the abolition of the group voting ticket system , which helped elect micro-party representatives with very small proportions of the vote, could make life easier for the next government.
Keep an eye out for whether the Coalition seems to be on track for a second seat in the Northern Metropolitan region or a third seat in Northern Victoria .
That would indicate the party are going to be in a strong enough position to avoid tricky multi-party negotiations and instead can go to any of Labor, One Nation, or the Greens to pass legislation.
A good night for both One Nation and the Greens would be winning a seat in every region, while a great night would be picking up even more.

items.title: MotoGP circuit to claim fewer trees as transplant solution offered
paras: Premier Peter Malinauskas said 94 trees will be transplanted to other parts of Adelaide's Park Lands. ( ABC News )
The SA Government will transplant 94 olive trees across the Park Lands instead of removing them for the MotoGP circuit design.
Premier Peter Malinauskas said experts have high confidence the "hardy species" will have a high survival rate.
South Australia's state government has reduced the number of trees to be removed for the controversial MotoGP circuit, with 94 olive trees to be "transplanted" across the Adelaide Park Lands.
The change means the total number of trees destroyed for the sporting event will be reduced to 288.
The olive trees are currently located between Wakefield Road and Bartels Road and will be transplanted to existing olive groves within the Park Lands.
Premier Peter Malinauskas said the project was worthy of pursuit, after seeking expert approval from arborists.
The state government says the species is 'hardy' and will have a high survival rate when transplanted. ( ABC News )
The premier said arborists provided a "high confidence" the hardy species would have a "very high survival rate".
"Some can be transplanted quickly subject to the identified locations, but others will be put into temporary storage arrangements in pots", Mr Malinauskas said.
The reduction in tree casualties comes after a long-running feud between activists and the Malinauskas government and a call from dozens of celebrities to halt the tree removal.
Two legal challenges almost placed roadblocks in the way of the MotoGP circuit construction, but those challenges fell over in the Supreme and Federal courts.
The premier confirmed the olive tree transplanting work would start next month.
The state government said it engaged extensively with the Adelaide City Council before confirming a solution.
Protesters watch as trees in Adelaide's parklands are removed for the MotoGP circuit construction in November. ( ABC News: Daniel Taylor )
Adelaide City Council Lord Mayor Jane Lomax-Smith welcomed the news saying the olive trees had historical significance.
"They really have followed the path of settlement in South Australia," she said.
"Clearly it's technically difficult … but we understand it's possible and it can be done."
The state government said that, including the olive trees, a total of 182 trees would be transplanted within the Park Lands.
New renders were released today to show which olive trees will be transplanted between Bartels and Wakefield roads.
The government released a new map in November 2026 to show which trees (in dark green) will be transplanted. ( Supplied: SA Government )

Outside of the motorsport event period, the government said this section of the Park Lands would feature 124 mature trees in planter boxes to become a new tree-lined connection for people walking and cycling between the city and the eastern suburbs.

items.title: Culture preserved in new Aboriginal language dictionaries
paras: Burchell Hayes with the Kurrama dictionary. ( ABC Pilbara: Kimberley Putland )
Linguists and traditional owners have created dictionaries for the Pinikura and Puutu Kunti Kurrama languages.
It's part of a project to engage community members with languages that are currently at risk of being lost.
Linguists are working on the next draft of the dictionaries, which will include more information from present-day speakers.
Two Aboriginal languages from Western Australia's Pilbara have been recorded and preserved in dictionaries for the first time, including one language with only three remaining fluent speakers.
The first drafts of the dictionaries were developed as part of a project by Puutu Kunti Kurrama and Pinikura (PKKP) Aboriginal Corporation to preserve Pinikura and Puutu Kunti Kurrama languages.
With both languages passed down through oral tradition, the dictionaries are the product of two years of collaboration between linguists and the remaining local speakers.
Pinikura traditional owner Terry Drage helped linguists with pronunciation.
"You can get a linguist to come in, and they will pronounce it their way," he said.
"And then that pronunciation, if we keep going with that type of pronunciation, then you lose [it]."
Terry (left) and Mitchell Drage believe the dictionaries could have an important role in the future. ( ABC Pilbara: Kimberley Putland )
Terry's brother, elder Mitchell Drage, is also a big advocate of the project.
Only three people speak Pinikura fluently, and Mitchell Drage would like that to change.
Linguist Breanna Kelly found documenting a language traditionally passed down orally one of the hardest parts of compiling the dictionary.
"A lot of the work that we do involves asking people questions to try and have them say some sentences back to us," she said.
"But we try to get information in different styles as much as we can, whether that's us just asking questions or whether it's more of a conversation, occasionally a bit of a role play."
Breanna Kelly hopes community members can use the dictionaries alongside online resources to learn the languages. ( ABC Pilbara: Amy Rossbach )
Ms Kelly said the team worked with present-day speakers and historical resources.
PKKP launched Pinikura and Kurrama language dictionaries at its 2026 AGM. ( ABC Pilbara: Kimberley Putland )
Burchell Hayes, a Puutu Kunti Kurrama descendant, said shame around getting the language wrong can be a barrier for younger Kurrama people wanting to learn it.
"We want them to identify themselves as Kurrama and be proud of who they are and be confident to be able to speak that language without that shame factor creeping in," Mr Hayes said.
He said it was why the first draft of the Kurrama dictionary is a good base, but not the final product.
Burchell Hayes says the release of the Kurrama dictionary is a proud moment. ( ABC Pilbara: Kimberley Putland )
The next drafts of the dictionaries are already underway, with plans to improve on the first editions by gathering feedback from community members.

items.title: RBI Issues Amendment Directions on ‘Suspected Money Mule Accounts to Prevent Cyber-enabled Financial Frauds’
paras: The Reserve Bank had issued the draft Reserve Bank of India (Know Your Customer) Amendment Directions, 2026 on September 11, 2026, for seeking feedback from stakeholders. The draft Amendment Directions proposed a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) laying down a uniform, time-bound procedure for banks to suo moto place temporary debit holds on amounts or accounts suspected to be linked to money mule activity and cyber-enabled financial frauds, and to remove such holds in coordination with Law Enforcement Agencies (LEAs), while protecting genuine customers from inconvenience. 2. Feedback received on the above draft Directions has been examined and the consequent modifications have been suitably incorporated in the final Amendment Directions. A statement on the feedback received is provided in the Annex . Accordingly, the Reserve Bank has today issued the following Amendment Directions, which shall come into effect from July 1, 2027, or from such earlier date as a bank may decide to implement the SOP. items.title: ED arrests six persons in cross-border drugs smuggling network
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): The Enforcement Directorate ( ED ) has arrested six persons in connection with an investigation under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) case linked to a cross-border drug smuggling network, the agency said on Tuesday. ED 's Delhi unit arrested these accused in different operations launched on October 11, October 18 and October 20. The arrested accused are identified as Lovejit Singh alias Labba, Manjeet Singh alias Manna, Prabhjit Singh, Gurjot Singh, Ramandeep Singh, and Gurpreet Singh. "A major drug trafficking operation involving smuggling of heroin from Afghanistan into India was unearthed during investigation," said the ED in a statement. The PMLA investigation was initiated on the basis of seizure of 293.81 kg of heroin from containers imported by Sandhu Exports at Nhava Sheva Port by the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence and seizure of 352.71 kg of heroin from two vehicles and a flat in Faridabad, Haryana, by the Delhi Police Special Cell. Thus, a total of 646.52 kg of heroin has been seized so far. ED investigation revealed that the arrested persons, Lovejit Singh, Manjeet Singh, Ramandeep Singh, Gurjot Singh, Gurpreet Singh and Prabhjit Singh, coordinated the smuggling, storage and distribution of heroin across Punjab, Haryana, and Delhi.

"These individuals were key members of a syndicate that smuggled heroin from Afghanistan and Iran, concealing them within shipments of talc stone and gypsum powder," said the ED . Accused persons incorporated Sandhu Exports, a front company owned by Prabhjit Singh, to carry out the smuggling of drugs, informed the federal agency. ED uncovered the highly sophisticated heroin smuggling and money laundering network where identification of multiple bank accounts, cash transactions, and operational expenses by the accused has been made. "Accused disguised the origin of the illicit funds, which were further layered and integrated into seemingly legitimate financial activities. It was also revealed that the syndicate did not make any payments to Afghan suppliers until the drugs were sold in local markets." Further, the agency said the accused used cash payments to purchase multiple vehicles including Toyota Fortuner, Etios and Hyundai Verna etc in second hand market for trafficking from the storage Hubs to further distribution. The ED investigation revealed that cash was used for the purchase of high-end smartphones and encrypted communication apps were used to coordinate smuggling activities. "Drugs smuggled from Iran and Afghanistan used to be imported via the Nava Sheva port in Mumbai, later stored at a rented godown in Shivpuri, Madhya Pradesh and further distributed for local supply in parts of Delhi, Punjab and Haryana. Transportation was carried out in lesser quantities of 10 kg to prevent detection by law enforcement agencies. Earlier, a property in Jandoli Village (Rajpura, Punjab), multiple bank accounts in the names of accused persons, and fixed deposits have been attached by ED ," added the agency. (ANI)

According to the central probe agency the accused persons incorporated Sandhu Exports, a front company owned by Prabhjit Singh, to carry out the smuggling of drugs. According to ED , the investigation under PMLA linked to a cross-border drugs smuggling network was initiated based on the seizure of 293.81 kg of heroin from containers imported by Sandhu Exports at Nhava Sheva Port by DRI and the seizure of 352.71 kg of heroin from two vehicles and a flat in Faridabad, Haryana by the Delhi Police Special Cell. Thus, a total of 646.52 Kg. of heroin has been seized so far. ED uncovered the highly sophisticated heroin smuggling and money laundering network where the identification of multiple bank accounts, cash transactions, and operational expenses by the accused has been made. The accused disguised the origin of the illicit funds, which were further layered and integrated into seemingly legitimate financial activities. It was also revealed that the syndicate did not make any payments to Afghan suppliers until the drugs were sold in the local market. Further, the accused used cash payments to purchase multiple vehicles in the second-hand market for trafficking from the storage hubs to further distribution. The ED investigation revealed that cash was used for the purchase of high-end smartphones and encrypted communication apps were used to coordinate smuggling activities. Drugs smuggled from Iran and Afghanistan used to be imported via Nava Sheva port in Mumbai, later stored at a rented godown in Shivpuri Madhya Pradesh, and further distributed for local supply in parts of Delhi, Punjab and Haryana. Transportation was carried out in lesser quantities of 10 kg to prevent detection by law enforcement agencies. Previously, a property in Jandoli Village (Rajpura, Punjab), multiple bank accounts in the names of accused persons, and fixed deposits were attached by the ED . (ANI)

items.title: Indian students in Kazan delighted as PM Modi arrives for BRICS Summit
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel Kazan [ Russia ], October 22 (ANI): Indian students in Kazan , Russia , are happy and excited about Prime Minister Narendra Modi's arrival at Hotel Korston , as he attends the 16th BRICS Summit . Notably, PM Narendra Modi on Tuesday touched down in Kazan city of Russia to participate in the 16th BRICS Summit and received a warm welcome. He is here to attend the 16th BRICS Summit , being held under the Chairmanship of Russia . To welcome PM Modi , students from India studying in Russia also sang a welcome song as they awaited PM Modi 's arrival at Hotel Korston . An Indian student from Pune, Saniya said that the students are quite excited to greet PM Modi . "Maybe we will get the opportunity (to meet PM Modi ) as many students are here (at Hotel Korston )... We are very excited. We are lucky to have this opportunity and we are happy to see him," she told ANI. An Indian student from Bihar, Shaurya Pratap said, "We are very happy to welcome PM Modi and we have prepared a song for him and we hope he likes it." Surbhi from Delhi said, "I have been here in Kazan since 2019 and today, we are going to sing a song for PM Modi and we are very excited about that." Parul, a final-year medical student, who has been in Kazan for the last five years told ANI, "We are really grateful that we got this opportunity to welcome our dear Prime Minister." Arti Pawar from Maharashtra said, "I have been living here for the past three years. I am very happy that PM Modi is coming here." Mrunmayi from Nagpur, Maharashtra said, "All the students here are quite enthusiastic as PM is going to come soon. We are too much delighted to welcome him." Meanwhile, ISKCON volunteers - from the Russia n and Indian communities were seen chanting 'Hare Krishna, Hare Ram' ahead of PM Modi 's arrival. While speaking with ANI, Sergoy, an ISKCON volunteer, said, "'Hare Krishna is a Mahamantra. This visit of PM Modi to Kazan , Russia is an important one for us. We are happy." Another ISKCON volunteer said, "We want to welcome PM Modi here in Kazan . It's a great honour for us to welcome him here We are very excited to see him." A Russia n citizen, Alexander said that the people there will welcome PM Modi by singing a song and that he is happy with PM Modi 's visit to Kazan . He said, "We have made a banner and we will also sing a song to welcome PM Modi ... I returned from India just two days back and directly came from Delhi to Kazan to see PM Modi . I am very happy that he is coming to Russia ." Notably, ahead of his departure to Russia , PM Modi shared a post on X and wrote, "Leaving for Kazan , Russia , to take part in the BRICS Summit . India attaches immense importance to BRICS, and I look forward to extensive discussions on a wide range of subjects. I also look forward to meeting various leaders there." The Prime Minister's office in a statement quoted PM Modi as saying, "I am departing today on a two-day visit to Kazan at the invitation of H.E. Mr. Vladimir Putin, President of the Russia n Federation, to attend the 16th BRICS Summit ." "India values the close cooperation within BRICS which has emerged as an important platform for dialogue and discussion on issues concerning the global developmental agenda, reformed multilateralism, climate change, economic cooperation, building resilient supply chains, promoting cultural and people to people connect, among others," PM Modi said. The statement further said that the expansion of BRICS with the addition of new members last year has added to its inclusivity and agenda for the global good. "Building upon the Annual Summit held in July 2024 in Moscow, my visit to Kazan will further reinforce the Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership between India and Russia . I look forward to meeting other leaders from BRICS as well," the PMO statement said. The 16th BRICS Summit in Kazan is being held under the chairmanship of Russia from October 22-24. During his visit, PM Modi is also expected to hold bilateral meetings with his counterparts from BRICS member countries and invited leaders in Kazan . The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said, "The Summit, themed 'Strengthening Multilateralism for Just Global Development and Security,' will provide an important platform for leaders to discuss key global issues." It further said, "The Summit will offer a valuable opportunity to assess the progress of initiatives launched by BRICS and to identify potential areas for future collaboration." This visit marks, PM Modi 's second visit to Russia this year. He travelled to Moscow in July to attend the 22nd India- Russia Annual Summit where he held a bilateral meeting with President Putin. He was also conferred with Russia 's highest civilian award, the Order of St. Andrew the Apostle at the Kremlin in Moscow. BRIC, as a formal grouping, started after the meeting of the Leaders of Russia , India and China in St Petersburg on the margins of G8 Outreach Summit in 2006. The grouping was formalized during the first meeting of BRIC Foreign Ministers on the margins of UNGA in New York in 2006. The first BRIC Summit was held in Russia 's Yekaterinburg in 2009. It was agreed to expand BRIC into BRICS with the inclusion of South Africa at the BRIC Foreign Ministers' meeting in New York in 2010. South Africa attended the 3rd BRICS Summit in Sanya in 2011. A further expansion of BRICS took place in 2024 with five new members - Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates. (ANI)

items.title: "Singapore plays key role in Act-East policy": Rajnath Singh at India-Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [ India ], October 22 (ANI): Dr. Ng Eng Hen , Singapore 's Minister of Defence , has begun his three-day visit to India . As part of his visit, Dr. Hen co-chaired the sixth India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue in New Delhi, with his India n counterpart Rajnath Singh . The Summit began on Tuesday morning, with India n Defence Minister Rajnath Singh welcoming the Singapore delegation warmly. He noted that the strategic partnership the two countries share is a "testimony of increasing closeness between our countries." Singh said, " The meeting is happening at a time when India marks the decade of India 's Act in Policy, in which Singapore has played a key role in promoting economic cooperation, cultural ties, and developed strategic connectivity with country institutions." Building upon Singh's remarks, Dr. Ng Eng Hen said, "You reminded us that this is the 10th year since your Act East Policy. From Singapore 's perspective, India has always been part of the East. Whether you choose to act or look, we consider you part of the area." He said that while remembering the history of Singapore , India has been an important partner. " When we started the Singapore armed forces, one of the countries that we asked early on to see whether they could help us was India ." Hen highlighted that such historical memoirs serve as important reminders and "reflects how we feel that India is very part of our area. We are delighted that our ten years of bilateral relations have been very much improved in defence and all-round strategic partnership." Hen also thanked PM Modi for visiting Singapore earlier this year and noted that the visit was an excellent meeting. A day before, the Ministry of Defence had announced the sixth India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue in New Delhi on October 22, 2024. The release noted that between India and Singapore , "The engagements have diversified to include wide-ranging contacts between the Services, military-to-military exchanges, high-level visits, capacity building and training programs, cooperation in UN Peacekeeping, ship visits and bilateral exercises." Inaugurated in 2016, the India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue is a key platform to strengthen bilateral defence cooperation between Singapore and India . The fifth edition of the Defence Ministers' Dialogue took place in January 2021 through virtual teleconference. During the meeting, the two parties showed confidence in the outcomes of the meeting that would result in providing impetus to the entire spectrum of the bilateral engagement as well as to the regional security architecture. (ANI)

items.title: "India matters most for future of planet" says British High Commissioner Lindy Cameron
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): In recent times when climate change has become a pressing issue with countries across the world being ravaged due to climate catastrophes, it becomes imperative to discuss and deliberate upon global actions that can help the world rise up and meet these challenges. At the NDTV World Summit's a discussion was held on the theme, "India Matters The Most For Future Of Planet". Participants in the discussion included Erik Solheim, Former Minister of Climate and the Environment of Norway; Lindy Cameron , British High Commissioner to India; Shishir Priyadarshi, President Chintan Research Foundation; Harjeet Singh, Global Engagement Director, Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty Initiative. "India is the country that matters the most for the future of the planet and climate change. India's ambition for development should not in any way be constrained by the responsibilities of the planet," Lindy Cameron , British High Commissioner to India, emphasised. She noted that the UK is committed towards the Multilateral Development Banks (MDB) reforms, technology and research support in India to aid the efforts. "Every dollar invested in resilient infrastructure pays 4 times over," said Cameron. "Lived experience of climate emergencies helps people to understand why their government needs to take policy action now," she added. Further talking about the need for urgent government action, Harjeet Singh, Global Engagement Director, Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty Initiative said, "Series of disasters affecting both developed and developing countries are serving as a wake-up call. As rich countries will get more and more affected by climate change which they did not imagine till a couple of years ago, most vulnerable countries are going to be struggling with impacts who also have very less capacity to deal with it. India is taking a leadership role in the global fight against climate change. Initiatives such as Global Biofuels Alliance, International Solar Alliance, and Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure are some efforts taken by India in recent years to manage the climate crisis. (ANI)

items.title: Asia's Largest Mindfulness India Summit 2024 Marks a New Era for Corporate Culture and Personal Well-being with the Inau
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel PNN Mumbai (Maharashtra) [India], October 22: The Mindfulness India Summit 2024, an initiative by the Mindful Science Centre, presented by HSBC and supported by CII Leadership and HR Committee, successfully concluded its two-day event on October 17 and 18, 2024, establishing new benchmarks in corporate culture and personal well-being. With over 40 international and national experts addressing mindfulness, emotional intelligence, and neuroscience, the summit highlighted how these principles are essential in transforming leadership, enhancing employee engagement, and fostering sustainable well-being within organizations. The evolving workplace landscape, particularly the increasing role of AI, requires a renewed focus on human-centric leadership and emotional resilience. The summit provided a platform for forward-thinking leaders to explore how mindfulness can effectively bridge this gap, ensuring both corporate excellence and employee well-being . The summit featured MasterChef Sanjeev Kapoor as the Chief Guest, who shared how mindful leadership has played a pivotal role in building his culinary empire. Along with Chris Ruane, Ex MP British Parliament and Chair of Mindfulness Initiative UK, J N Behl and Global Holistic Health Guru Mickey Mehta, Kapoor also launched Manish Behl's new book "Observe - 101 Mindfulness Practices", a guide designed to make mindfulness accessible for both professionals and individuals in their everyday lives. Behl, a global mindfulness expert and founder of the Mindful Science Centre, shared, "With this book, I want to demystify mindfulness and make it accessible to everyone. Mindfulness is not a complex or distant concept, but a practical tool for reducing stress, improving focus, and fostering deeper connections in both personal and professional settings." The Mindfulness India Summit 2024 has successfully proven that mindfulness is no longer a luxury but a necessity in modern corporate structures. By adopting mindfulness practices, organizations are not only creating more compassionate work environments but are also enhancing their overall performance and sustainability in a world increasingly shaped by technological and emotional complexity. The 2 days also saw the launch of Mindfulness Impact Awards, to honor organizations and individuals who have integrated mindfulness into their corporate structures and personal lives. These awards reflect the growing recognition that workplace culture directly affects employee productivity, creativity, and overall well-being. Manish Behl, founder of the awards, explained, "Corporate success today goes beyond profit; it's about fostering environments where employees thrive mentally, emotionally, and physically. Our vision with these awards is to inspire a deeper integration of mindfulness in corporate cultures worldwide. By recognizing these pioneers, we hope these awards inspire companies and individuals to further integrate mindfulness into their environments, ultimately fostering happier, more productive workplaces, communities, and a more compassionate world." The awards were designed to acknowledge champions of mindfulness across categories, recognizing those who incorporate mindful practices to improve workplace culture, employee engagement, and societal impact. Winners ranged from corporate giants like Aditya Birla Group and Accenture to global educators and community leaders. items.title: "No shortage of oil in world and prices should hopefully come down", says Hardeep Singh Puri
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): Hardeep Singh Puri, Minister for Petroleum and Natural Gas on Tuesday said that there is no shortage of oil in the world and prices will come down soon, answering the question of the recent upswing in crude oil prices. Speaking to the media, the Union Minister cited global factors such as the war in the Middle East and voluntary cuts in oil production which are influencing the oil prices in the global market. He said, "It depends on global factors. One thing is very clear, there is no shortage of oil in the world...Today, more and more oil is coming on the market...There are other factors like geopolitical tensions. So, there is no shortage of oil but if there is tension in one part of the world, then the freight cost, and insurance freight cost will go up. Today, let us all hope that better sense prevails, that call for peace that our Prime Minister has been making from every forum...There is more than enough oil in the world and prices should hopefully come down. That's my expectation..." "If there's tension in one part of the world, then the cost of, if you have to take a longer route, then the cost of the freight cost, the insurance rate cost, that will go up...There's more than enough oil in the world, and prices should hopefully come down," he commented in his personal capacity.

The union minister said many countries such as Brazil, and Guayana among others are coming with their oil. Citing the stable prices in the last 3 years, the minister said that the government is taking every possible step to ensure stable oil prices. "Central government at every stage has stepped in to cushion and bring the prices down from November 2021 to May 2022. Now there are some global factors. The cost at the retail point is determined by the cost of the barrel in the international market plus the cost of transportation, freight, insurance, retailers, refining cost and margin, then dealers, margin, etc. We are solving all the problems we can, now you tell the global community to hold and bring them down," he added. This comes after oil prices rose nearly 2 per cent on Monday, reclaiming major losses from last week's sell-off. Brent crude features upped by $1.44, or 1.97 per cent in the afternoon. Earlier this month, Puri had said that the country is well-prepared to meet its growing energy demands, with a diverse range of oil sources. Speaking on the availability of oil in the global market, Puri emphasised that India has expanded its procurement base, moving from 27 suppliers to 39. (ANI)

items.title: November 28, 1999: The day Pete Sampras won the ATP Finals for the fifth time
paras: Every day, Tennis Majors takes you back to one of the most iconic moments in tennis history. On this day in 1999, Pete Sampras equaled Ivan Lendl’s record for the most season-ending ATP Finals titles won

On this day, November 28, 1999, Pete Sampras won the season-ending ATP Finals for the fifth time, tying Ivan Lendl’s record at the time. To achieve this feat, he defeated Andre Agassi in the final (6-1, 7-5, 6-4), although his long-time rival had outplayed him during the round-robin phase (6-2, 6-2).

For Sampras, it was a great way to finish a complicated year, during which he had to skip both the Australian Open and the US Open because of injuries and had lost his world No 1 spot. As for Agassi, who was enjoying the best season of his career, it was a reminder that his old rival would always be there to challenge him in the big events.

Friendships are built by repeated contact, not by being liked
items.hook: This is the single most useful fact in the whole guide.
paras: Studies of primary-school classrooms found that children seated next to each other were far more likely to become friends than children seated across the room. When teachers changed the seating, new friendships formed with the new neighbours.

So the engine is: same place, same people, same activity, over and over. The day at the yo-yo bar followed by basketball is that engine working - shared activity changed how the other boy treated him. It was not luck.
items.do: Pick one activity he already likes and commit to it weekly for a full term.

items.title: Keep the proximity - change the watching
items.hook: Your instinct is half right, and the other half matters.
paras: You are right that being around the group matters: children nominate as friends the children they see and interact with most. 'Out of sight, out of mind' is real for acquaintances.

But guidance written for schools is blunt: merely remaining beside a group is not friendship. A child who hovers is read as a bystander rather than a player, and it holds him in the one-down position. Watching has a use - but only as the first twenty seconds of joining in, never as the endpoint.
items.do: Keep telling him to stay near the group. Add: 'then take a job in the game'.

items.title: Teach 'watch, then blend'
items.hook: The best way to join a game is not to ask.
paras: Most of us were told to walk up and say 'Can I play?' But that makes everyone stop and look at him, and makes 'no' very easy.

The better sequence, used by people who study play: watch for about twenty seconds to learn the game and where the line is, then slide into the action without stopping it. Take the end of the line. Stand in the outfield. Pick up the ball and pass it back.
items.do: Rehearse it at home in five minutes. Ask him to name the 'easiest job' in each game.

items.title: Host one friend at a time - this is the biggest lever you control
items.hook: The child who invites is rarely short of friends.
paras: Pick a child he has had fun with in the last month, not someone he admires from afar. Invite one person for one to two hours. Put away anything precious, have two activities ready, start with a snack, and let the guest choose sometimes.
Keep it short and end while they are both still enjoying it. Then leave a few weeks before inviting the same child again, so the invitation can come back to him.
items.do: Text one parent this week and set a date for the school holidays.

items.title: Ask the teacher one specific question
items.hook: Teachers see the playground. Ask them to name names.
paras: Ask two things: who does he play well with, and could he be seated near them or paired with them for group work?
Seating is one of the few levers that reliably creates new friendships, and it is invisible to the children - no one has to know it was arranged.
items.do: Email the teacher this week with those two questions.

items.title: Do not push into a group that is rejecting him
items.hook: Here the advice is the opposite of persistence.
paras: Where a group is actively excluding him, the guidance is to back off - when you back off from people, they can move towards you. Put his energy into two or three other children instead of one closed circle.
Friends in more than one place - school, a club, family friends - also make him far less vulnerable when one group turns cold.
items.do: Help him list three children outside the difficult group he could get to know.

items.title: One or two good friends is the goal - not popularity
paras: Kids need one or two good friends. You do not need to worry about him being the most popular child in the class.
His warmth and kindness are already the raw material. Treat this as coaching a skill, not fixing a fault - if he feels like a project, he will resist.
items.do: Say his strengths out loud, often. Confidence is what carries a child into a group.

items.title: Playing and talking with girls is normal and good
items.hook: Children believe gender matters far more than it actually does.
paras: In one large classroom experiment, simply seating boys and girls next to each other doubled how often they became friends.
Girls' play tends to build conversation, turn-taking and inventing games together; boys' play builds bigger, faster group play. Being good at both widens his circle.
items.do: No action needed. Just do not let him think it is odd.

items.title: When to get more help
items.hook: Ordinary friendship difficulty is not a disorder.
paras: Get more support if he becomes reluctant to go to school, is persistently distressed, has changes in sleep or appetite, or says it is happening all the time and he cannot make it stop.
Start with his teacher, then the school counsellor, then your GP for a referral. Kids Helpline is free and open 24/7 on 1800 55 1800, for children and for parents.
items.do: Save Kids Helpline in your phone: 1800 55 1800.
